summary: Clean 100/100 migration; no parity defects. Applied two surgical, generalizable skill-defect fixes around the WinAppSDK analyzer's WUI1xxx interop-advisory family (WUI1001 pickers), which the skill neither documented nor distinguished from the fatal WUI000x runtime-crash class.

changes.section: WUI analyzer warnings — two classes, handled differently (was: 'WUI analyzer warnings (UWP API residue)')
changes.edit: Split into Class 1 WUI000x (UWP-only API residue, MUST fix) and Class 2 WUI1xxx interop/modernization advisories (e.g. WUI1001 pickers). Documented that WUI1001 persists on the WinRT picker type even after InitializeWithWindow is applied (syntactic rule) and is benign — do not chase or revert working interop. Scoped the 'no false positives' claim to WUI000x. Cross-referenced #pickers. Noted winapp build is the authoritative WUI surface vs a plain dotnet build.
changes.general_rule: WinAppSDK WUIxxxx warnings are two classes: WUI000x = UWP-only API residue that throws at runtime (fix it); WUI1xxx = interop/modernization advisories that are benign once the documented interop pattern is applied and may keep firing regardless — never revert working code to silence them.

changes.section: Section 6 dotnet build healthcheck — WUI warning classification
changes.edit: Partitioned WUI warnings into $wuiFatal (WUI000x) and $wuiAdvisory (other WUIxxxx). FAIL only on WUI000x; report WUI1xxx advisories via a [WARN] line. Updated comments to name winapp build as the authoritative WUI surface. Verified PARSE OK.
changes.general_rule: The validator must fail only on runtime-crash residue (WUI000x); a correct picker/share/print migration that follows the skill's interop pattern will legitimately emit WUI1xxx advisories and must not be failed for them.

changes.edit: Reworded 'zero WUI analyzer warnings' to 'zero WUI000x (UWP-only API residue) warnings; benign WUI1xxx interop advisories (e.g. picker WUI1001) are WARN, not FAIL — do not chase', with a link to the reworked PATTERNS.md section.
changes.general_rule: Same two-class distinction, surfaced at the point where the agent reads the validation gate expectations.

rejected_or_deferred.item: Force the validator's dotnet build to enable the full winapp analyzer ruleset
rejected_or_deferred.reason: Higher risk / speculative; not evidenced to be needed this run (validator's dotnet build already reported 0 WUI). Two-class partition is the surgical fix.

rejected_or_deferred.item: Recommend switching pickers to Microsoft.Windows.Storage.Pickers to eliminate WUI1001
rejected_or_deferred.reason: New API with version constraints; optional, not required for parity. Documented as optional rather than mandated to avoid over-reach.
Scenario-specific benign warnings, no parity impact — dev-agent-slip, not generalizable.

devils_advocate: Score was 100, so no change is strictly required by outcome. But the WUI1001 evidence is concrete (appeared in the actual winapp build on correctly-migrated, working picker code), pickers recur across most UWP samples, and the current docs+validator would actively mislead a future agent into chasing or reverting a benign warning. The falsifiable check: if a future picker migration emits WUI1001, the reworked skill now tells the agent it is benign and the validator no longer FAILs it — without weakening the WUI000x runtime-crash gate.
